question: on a fixed sample of the c2 train-split games: how much does an S400 re-search change the raw visit distributions and the policy targets of the c2 rule against S200 (beside S50 -> S200), and what does a full re-search cost
scope: a measurement only: no training, no Arena, no reading or pass rule; the decision on a full re-search and a training contract is the user's
models_note: the parent pair that played the c2 self-play (h7c_retarget.check_engine refuses any other); not c5
budget_rule: fixed here; never read from a cycle decision (h7c_retarget run reads the cycle-1 decision, which gives S200)

sample.source: the c2 policy rows: game ids of rows with split train (games the label step kept after the probe drops; split_for salt h7c-v1, val 5%)
sample.order: sha256("<salt>:<game id>") ascending, then the id; the first `games`; the first `early_check_games` of that order are the early S200 check
sample.positions: every eligible ply (actor target kind visits) of the sampled games; the count comes from the coverage list fixed by prepare (about 2,090 is a planning value)

reproduction.what: the sample re-searched at S200 against the c2 S200 records
reproduction.rule_source: the G0 rule of h7c_retarget (mean values are stored rounded to 6 decimals)
order: S200 on the first 5 sample games, checked
S200 on the other 95, the whole sample checked
S400 on the whole sample, only after both checks
reproduction.miss: stop and record (measure.json status S200_EARLY_NOT_REPRODUCED / S200_NOT_REPRODUCED); no S400; nothing is relaxed

metrics.raw: root visit counts normalised over every visited move (nothing removed): top-1 change, total variation, Jensen-Shannon (base 2), entropy (bits), top share, visited children; proven-loss set relation (same / first only / second only / both unique)
metrics.target: the c2 rule (h7c_retarget.retarget_target: visits without the union of the actor's and the search's proven losses): top-1 change, total variation, Jensen-Shannon, entropy, KL(target || H3) with the training encoding and legal mask
pairs: S50 -> S200 (reference: what c2 trained on)

populations.target_pair: unmasked c2 rows where both budgets of the pair leave a target
populations.target_common: unmasked c2 rows where S50, S200 and S400 all leave a target (the same positions for both pairs)

metrics.denominators: masked rows, positions without a c2 row, target none per budget, S200-only and S400-only targets, pair and common counts are reported beside the tables
metrics.top1_ties: the first move in row-major order
metrics.aggregate: position-weighted mean, median, 90th percentile; per move bucket

bootstrap.statistic: position-weighted mean of the drawn games' positions

time_scopes.full_re_search: every eligible ply of the c2 games: what h7c_retarget run searches and h7c_labels --retarget requires
time_scopes.training_data: the eligible plies of the train-split games the label step kept

time_estimates: ratio: c2 S200 wall x (sample S400 / S200 search seconds) x (scope / eligible)
extrapolation: sample S400 wall x scope / sample positions (only when no search phase resumed)
search only: sample S400 search seconds per position x scope / workers
check: the sample S200 wall extrapolated to all eligible plies against the actual c2 wall
planning_values: about 40 minutes for the sample and 4.2 hours for a full S400 re-search are plan values, replaced by the measurement

identity.experiment_sha256: sha256 of the canonical JSON of this contract without "approved"

invariance: HEAD (clean), the contract file, the sources and the inputs at the start, checked again right before publishing
